title: Hungary
capsule: After the 1946 abolition of the monarchy and proclamation of a short-lived Second Republic, Hungary's Communist Party under Mátyás Rákosi consolidated one-party rule by 1949, renaming the state the Hungarian People's Republic. The 1956 uprising against Soviet domination was crushed by Soviet tanks, ushering in János Kádár's more moderate 'goulash communism' before the 1989 round-table talks dismantled one-party rule and restored a democratic republic; Hungary joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004, and since 2010 has been governed by Viktor Orbán's increasingly illiberal Fidesz government.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territory of interwar Hungary is precisely defined by the Treaty of Trianon and the Vienna Awards, with boundary lines documented in international treaty instruments; the dataset label 'Hungarian Republic' is a misnomer for the Kingdom of Hungary under regency.
